title: Near-Optimal Parallel Approximate Counting via Sampling
summary: The computational equivalence between approximate counting and sampling is well established for polynomial-time algorithms. The most efficient general reduction from counting to sampling is achieved via simulated annealing, where the counting problem is formulated in terms of estimating the ratio $Q={Z(β_{\max})}/{Z(β_{\min})}$ between partition functions $Z(β)=\sum_{x\in Ω} \exp(βH(x))$ of Gibbs distributions $μ_β$ over $Ω$ with Hamiltonian $H$, given access to a sampling oracle that produces samples from $μ_β$ for $β\in [β_{\min}, β_{\max}]$.
